label: Possible not to be: in the subject or through another's power
term: possible not to be (potency to non-being in the subject versus another's power over its esse)
resolution: Q.9 a.2 calls creatures 'possible not to be' in two ways: through a potency in the thing itself, and through a power in another (the creator's power over their esse). DEF-CAN-FAIL-TO-BE does not itself say 'in the subject'. The C2 batch reads CanFailToBe x esse as the in-subject channel only (POSSIBLE_NOT_TO_BE_1: corruptible simply, a two-way potency in the thing to be and not be), and represents possibility of non-being through another's power by PowerOverEsse (POSSIBLE_NOT_TO_BE_2), not by CanFailToBe. The power-grounding premise (PGP) is the disjunction of the two senses; the correlation premise relates sense 2 to sense 1 or to CAUSE_2 at esse as an explicit OPEN premise. Consequence: under this reading Aquinas denies #1870's B4a (every being contingent at w can fail to be in substance) for angels, which on q.50 a.5 have no potency to non-being although they are possible not to be through the creator's power. No argument passes silently between the two senses.
